items.title: Capture immutable starting roster and sign-up snapshots automatically
items.notes: Collaborator implementation in progress per maintainer; no PR recorded yet. Capture at scheduled start; handle retries, cancellation and rescheduling. Never rewrite the original snapshot. Not deployed.

items.title: Display historical raid rosters separately from live team assignments
items.notes: Show the starting snapshot without implying that sign-ups prove attendance.

items.title: Support audited in-raid roster changes
items.notes: Leader adjustments must not overwrite the starting snapshot.

items.title: Add leader benching, capacity and raid-spot priority workflows
items.notes: Distinguish voluntary and involuntary benches. Agree capacity and Casual/Hardcore allocation policy before implementation.

items.title: Record attendance and show rolling three-month reporting
items.notes: GitHub issue #22 (B7) is assigned to stewartalex4-art; preserve that claim and coordinate before starting. Assignment alone is not evidence of implementation or a RAID-001 snapshot claim. Record actual attendance, roll alts up to mains, preserve the December 9 baseline, and agree bench counting. Members see their own percentage; leaders see everyone. Audited attendance corrections and distinct voluntary/involuntary benches remain required.

items.title: Send raid creation, 24-hour and 1-hour reminders
items.notes: Agree delivery channels and use reliable scheduled server work.

items.title: Build raid buff and debuff coverage checklist
items.notes: GitHub issue #16 covers the delivered first checklist; #27 tracks recurring data verification and remains actionable despite its earlier closure. Checklist for 10/20/40-player teams deployed in ec45641, with confidence-labelled estimates, spell details and provider/source panel. Remaining: verify provisional/unverified Forever game data, unresolved scope/exclusivity mechanics and missing descriptions; recheck at beta end, launch week and December 9. Deployment does not mean game facts are confirmed.

items.title: Fix ten-zone audited raid edit expression-budget failure
items.notes: Deployed and verified before this cumulative release summary. Reduced validator cost without changing the ten-zone limit, authorization or audit checks. Regression coverage includes ten-zone creation, complete edits, cancellation/restore, malformed snapshots and forged audits.

items.title: Add All characters / Hide alts filter to the Raid Teams available roster
items.notes: Integrated through PR #65 and first deployed in 79736d9; included in the f42a14d release summary. Filters only the available roster and Add from guild roster lists using existing main/alt links. Assigned alts remain visible. Saved assignments, assigned team counts and buff/debuff coverage calculations remain unchanged.

items.title: Prevent same-player characters sharing a 10-player raid team
items.notes: Added to the canonical backlog during release reconciliation; source GitHub issue #95 (B10), implemented by stewartalex4-art in #110 and deployed in d0ef75d with live assets verified. Member picker, dropdown and drag-and-drop refuse main/alt and sibling-alt conflicts with an explanatory dialog and no write. Existing assignments remain unchanged, with conflicts highlighted. Different players' alts can share a team. Checks use stable roster IDs and main/alt links. Client-side validation only: optional Firestore enforcement was not implemented; stale concurrent clients or direct writes can bypass the check. No sign-up restriction or automatic cleanup.

items.title: Complete audited loot write helpers and enforcement
items.notes: Audited priority/award writes, phase changes and permanent readable Log deployed with matching rules and client. Unlogged write exceptions and local-preview import retired. Immutable award snapshots remain protected. Standalone manual awards and correction/removal controls remain LOOT-002/004.

items.title: Record manual awards without requiring priority listings
items.notes: Validated no-priority award rules are live, including stable recipient ID, decision, phase, raid date and atomic audit entry. LOOT-003 roster selection is now released. Remaining: standalone recording form and client helper without a priority. Awards through a priority note do not complete this standalone workflow. Spreadsheet receipts remain the fallback.

items.title: Select loot recipients and candidates by stable roster identity
items.notes: GitHub issue #12 (A3), resolved by the released roster-picker workflow. Deployed through edb344a and included in this verified cumulative release. Roster-picked candidates and award recipients carry stable character IDs; completion, filters and My dashboard follow recorded IDs through renames. Award candidate-order and council-note snapshots remain immutable, and historical award/Log names are retained. Legacy priorities convert on leader edit; unmatched names remain notes. Older name-only awards are not retroactively rewritten. Standalone no-priority awards remain LOOT-002.

items.title: Add award correction and removal UI and readable audit history
items.notes: GitHub issue #11 (A2) spans released LOOT-001 and this remaining scope; keep it open until award correction/removal acceptance is met. Readable permanent Log and legacy award history deployed in 92dbc71. Remaining: Guild/Raid Leader award correction and reason-required removal UI. No hard deletion; immutable decision snapshots must remain unchanged.

items.title: Import spreadsheet and addon awards with validated preview
items.notes: GitHub issue #21 (B6) spans this import scope and standalone manual entry in LOOT-002; neither is completed by awards through priority notes. Agree formats, duplicate detection and recipient matching. Preserve original award dates separately from later entry/audit timestamps. Support recovery of December 9 spreadsheet receipts. Preview must mark errors/duplicates and require confirmation; every import is audited and manual entry must work without external lookup.

items.title: Complete main/alt priority policy and alt-only-run controls
items.notes: Priority adoption is expected around December 15. Confirm wording and per-raid exception; priorities are not required for initial loot recording.

items.title: Add item/loot-table data and remaining priority filters
items.notes: GitHub issue #18 (B3) remains open for only-items-with-a-priority and remaining combined-filter acceptance; the older class-filter requirement was replaced by the approved toolbar design. Deployed through d0ef75d: Browse drops, live Wowhead names/icons/tooltips, item-based priority creation, dungeon/boss grouping, slot/encounter/player/completion filters, phase-specific zone selection and shared zone colors. Settings Zones supplies dungeon and raid catalog entries to scheduling and drop lists. Class/Needs players toolbar filters were replaced; Needs players remains a row marker. Remaining: only-items-with-a-priority filter and confirmation of complete Forever loot data. Nine bundled dungeons remain beta practice data, not game-verified facts.

items.title: Let leaders edit loot tables in the app, with import and audit
items.notes: GitHub issue #97 (B11) is superseded by the deployed phase-zone design, not implemented literally: checklists live in the drop-list editor, phases start empty unless Follows is explicit, and no old Show all requirement is asserted complete. Phase-specific guild drop-list editing and atomic audit enforcement deployed. Through d0ef75d: Guild/Raid Leaders paste item IDs or Wowhead links with name previews, add/reorder creatures and add/remove/restore items; phase zone checklists use the Settings Zones catalog. Earlier phases retain their lists. Remaining: full capture-file import with validated preview and any outstanding item move/replace workflow acceptance. Bundled source files remain unchanged.

items.title: Add items from Browse drops to the priority list and assign players
items.notes: Verified cumulative delivery: individual/bulk Browse drops priority creation, one item per phase, ordered stable-roster candidates including repeated characters, editable/finishable note lines and awards through notes. Taking assigned items off retains players/notes/awards for restoration. Edit Prio has pinned actions and unsaved-change confirmation; per-item ordering is locked by default. Carry-over provenance and confirmed audited removal are available; typed-by-hand priorities have their own removal group. Remaining loot-data/filter research stays open in LOOT-007 and is not implied complete by this workflow release.

items.title: Let leaders upload zone artwork and choose a picture for each zone
items.notes: Proposed mapping (GitHub issue #115): the maintainer confirms the ID, priority and target. Guild Leaders upload pictures (JPEG, PNG or WebP) to the guild's own Cloud Storage and choose one for each zone; a zone's picture is a banner on its title in Loot priorities, Browse drops and the drop-list editor, so a new raid needs a picture and a pick, not a release. Delivered as two PRs. Rules PR #116 (storage.rules and settings/zoneArt with tests) is merged and its Firestore and Storage rules are deployed, with Cloud Storage on and the Storage service agent granted Firestore access (maintainer handoff on #116; no authenticated production upload test yet). The app PR #117 (Settings > Zone images, the Artwork dropdown, the title banners) is open and not merged or deployed; production runs a mixed client/backend state until it ships. No picture is added to the repository (CONTRIBUTING: do not add other Blizzard assets); leaders upload them. Before the client deploy confirm the bucket name matches the build (VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET if it is not <project>.firebasestorage.app). Not planned: per-boss pictures.

items.title: Add Removed member status and no-access screen
items.notes: GitHub issue #14 (A5), resolved by #75. Deployed in a36ba48 and verified; included in this cumulative release summary. Guild Leader-only removal/restoration with confirmation, no self-removal, atomic unlinking, backend access denial and live no-access screen. Characters, assignments, history and Auth account remain. Restoration grants unlinked Member access, requiring explicit relinking/promotion.

items.title: Add character-change requests and leader approvals
items.notes: Deployed in 0c8c9c9 and production-confirmed by maintainer; included in the 92dbc71 summary. Members submit/withdraw private alt-link, rename, class/spec and main-promotion requests. Guild Leader review moved from Member access to Leadership Overview in the 2026-10-18 release (MEMBER-003); members retain personal requests on My dashboard. Atomic approvals recheck ownership/snapshots and preserve IDs, teams and history. Decisions are in resolved history, without automatic notification. Stable-ID loot now follows renames (LOOT-003); legacy name-only records are not retroactively migrated.

items.title: Build leadership dashboard with per-character raid readiness
items.notes: Scope approved in #106; #108 deployed with rules before Hosting in b31493a; #111 confirmation deployed in d0ef75d, with live assets verified. Guild Leader-only Leadership Overview between Loot priorities and Member access: summary counts, missing responses, private character-request review and selected-raid current-assignment coverage with 10/20/40 selector. Per-character readiness defaults false; members manage main/direct alts on My dashboard, Guild Leaders manage flags in roster. Confirm saves; Cancel leaves the flag unchanged. Exact-field writes and reciprocal ownership are enforced by Firestore rules. Count each active linked account once when any owned character is ready; any response counts, with separate unready-attending warnings. Excluded/setup counts and coverage uncertainty remain visible. No sign-up restrictions, reminders, attendance, automatic benching or starting snapshots. Roster comments remain MEMBER-004.

items.title: Review dashboard comments from the roster
items.notes: Deployed first in 537f5d8 and confirmed by the maintainer; included in the ec45641 release summary. Show Comments provides read-only Public/Leadership review with floating full-text panels. Authors edit on the dashboard; existing backend permissions remain enforced. Scroll dismissal follow-up is UX-003.

items.title: Edit owned unavailable date ranges without delete-and-recreate
items.notes: Reconciled from GitHub issue #96 (A7), not implemented. Edit from My dashboard and Raid Calendar using a prefilled dialog and an ownership/range-validated server callable. Atomically preserve raid-response consistency across old/new overlapping ranges; add server tests and deploy Functions before Hosting. Unscheduled pending prioritization; the older issue's proposed date is not a new commitment.

items.title: Complete approved readability and contrast pass
items.notes: GitHub issue #23 (B8). Review screenshots before applying the broader styling pass; verify light/dark contrast, focus/control visibility, phone layouts and input sizing. Localized recent styling changes do not complete the broader pass. Canonical target remains December 22, not the older issue's proposed date.

items.title: Make mobile help and core workflows touch-accessible
items.notes: November 4 adoption priority. Deployed in f42a14d: separate Casual/Hardcore help, tappable attendance chip, tap/keyboard coverage details and roster comments, mobile blank-space and narrow-header fixes. Reading help does not change raider type. Desktop Edge and mobile touch emulation checked. Remaining: physical-device/browser checks, keyboard-open forms/dialogs, orientation and broader core-workflow/touch-target validation. Keep separate from the contrast pass.

items.title: Standardize tooltip behavior and dismiss on scroll or other actions
items.notes: Shared HelpPopover and architecture/contributor interaction contract deployed in f42a14d for roster comments, dashboard help and coverage icon/status details. One-open behavior and dismissal on outside interaction, Escape, focus leaving, navigation, page/nested scrolling and viewport changes checked in desktop Edge/mobile touch emulation. Internal panel scrolling and fixed row heights preserved; PR #68 interactive sort dialog compatibility verified. Remaining: physical-device/browser acceptance checks.

items.title: Resolve full-character-name display and ambiguous legacy matching
items.notes: GitHub issue #109 (B12) is a research inventory, not an approved implementation plan. Blocked on maintainer decisions: first-name-only versus full-name UI, narrow layouts, duplicate full-name disambiguation, legacy matching and stored-versus-displayed names. Audit ambiguous legacy identity resolution without assuming surnames solve identity. Preserve immutable award/Log snapshots; do not rewrite historical text or change rules without approved scope. No owner or implementation claimed; unscheduled.

items.title: Build raid bot identity linking, announcements and sign-ups
items.notes: Verify interaction signatures and enforce existing ownership, unavailable-date, cancellation and cutoff guarantees. Decide two-way message updates. Separate from developer backlog publishing.

items.title: Resolve live-client addon research and exchange formats
items.notes: Probe exists. Still confirm messaging, master loot, journal data and invites; specify versioned roster/priority and award exchange formats.

items.title: Build production loot-master addon and award exchange
items.notes: Priority display, received marks, reliable award capture and app import/export.

items.title: Add raider responses, council voting and addon extras
items.notes: Web voting fallback if messaging fails; alt mapping, boss identification, roster invites and boss-level attendance. Acceptance scope needs agreement.

items.title: Define and build desktop-helper automation
items.notes: Research-stage saved-variable exchange; agree feasibility, safe local access and acceptance scope before implementation.

items.title: Integrate Warcraft Logs when Forever support is available
items.notes: External service support is unconfirmed. Raise the risk to the December 22 full-rollout target rather than promising unavailable integration.

items.title: Deliver on-request Discord backlog publisher
items.notes: Local tool adopted on the designated publishing machine. Live POST and PATCH verified during approved announcements; receipts saved locally. Adoption recorded in the f42a14d summary, not a Firebase feature deployment. Person-authored messages remain untouched.

items.title: Publish shared backlog and release notes to separate Discord channels
items.notes: Named destinations and coordinated shared-source publication adopted; maintainer confirmed correct channels on the first live run, and later approved publication edited existing backlog messages successfully. Receipts and credentials remain on one designated machine. This is an on-request developer publisher, not the planned raid bot.

items.title: Confirm billing alerts and initial absence synchronization
items.notes: GitHub issue #24 (C1) covers the billing subset; do not close it until the budget alert is verified. Operational verification, not new feature development. Blaze and Functions are deployed; budget alert and one-time backfill completion are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Rehearse first-raid readiness and spreadsheet recovery
items.notes: Check scheduled start capture, real-role authorization and failure handling. Rehearse spreadsheet recording if loot tooling is not ready; validate recovery upload once available. Separate from GitHub issue #26's earlier dungeon-loot dry-run (OPS-004).

items.title: Verify console safeguards and pre-migration Firestore export
items.notes: Reconciled from GitHub issue #25 (C2). Owner records evidence for Dependabot alerts, deployed-rules parity, Auth password/email-enumeration settings and a Firestore export before the first data migration. Consider optional main branch protection separately. Do not infer console settings or backup completion from a successful deployment; retain evidence outside public source if sensitive. Unscheduled pending prioritization.

items.title: Agree and run the launch dungeon-loot dry-run checklist
items.notes: Reconciled from GitHub issue #26 (C3), distinct from the December 9 first-raid rehearsal in OPS-002. Agree a checklist and record first-run findings: record/correct an award, inspect audit history/priorities, remove access and change season text. Award correction is not yet delivered (LOOT-004); do not report the full exercise complete from isolated smoke checks. Unscheduled pending prioritization; no dry-run completion verified.
